name: Total Knee and Total Hip Arthroplasty Rehabilitation
summary: Joint replacement replaces damaged joint surfaces with artificial components for advanced osteoarthritis or other joint destruction. Modern enhanced recovery pathways mobilise patients on the day of surgery or the next day, with short hospital stays.

Pre-operative exercise may modestly improve early function.
redFlags: Sudden hip pain, leg shortened and rotated after a movement (THA)

Knee flexion not improving by the early weeks after TKA
firstSteps: Discharge when safe with home exercise.

measures: Range, TUG, 30 s chair stand, 6MWT, stair climb test, Oxford Knee or Hip Score, KOOS or HOOS.

book.title: Total Knee and Total Hip Arthroplasty Rehabilitation

blocks.text: Joint replacement replaces damaged joint surfaces with artificial components for advanced osteoarthritis or other joint destruction. Modern **enhanced recovery** pathways mobilise patients on the day of surgery or the next day, with short hospital stays [Ref – to verify].

sections.title: B to C. Pre-operative education and assessment

blocks.text: Explain the plan, practise exercises and walking aids before surgery, assess home (stairs, toilet height, support). Pre-operative exercise may modestly improve early function [Ref – to verify].
Vital signs, pain, wound, neurovascular check (especially peroneal nerve after TKA; sciatic after THA), calf, range of motion, quadriceps activation, transfers, gait, stairs.

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Sudden hip pain, leg shortened and rotated after a movement (THA)
Calf pain and swelling, sudden breathlessness
Knee flexion not improving by the early weeks after TKA
Inform surgeon; manipulation under anaesthesia may be considered

steps: **Day 0 to 1:** check stability; sit, stand, walk with a frame.
**Progress** to crutches or stick, stairs, independent transfers.
**Outpatient:** range, strength, function, return to activities.

rows: Heel prop, quadriceps sets, prone hang
Heel slides, seated knee bends, stationary bike (start rocking, then full revolutions)
Functional targets: about 90 degrees for stairs and chair, more for some tasks [Ref – to verify]
SLR, sit-to-stand, step-ups, leg press, progressive resistance
Quadriceps weakness persists for months if not trained
Gluteal sets, bridging, standing hip abduction and extension, sit-to-stand, step-ups
Hip abductors are key for gait
Walking with aid, progress to no aid when limp-free
Depend on surgical approach (for example posterior approach: avoid combined flexion past 90 degrees, adduction and internal rotation for an agreed period)
Many centres now use reduced precautions; follow the surgeon [Ref – to verify]

blocks.text: Ice and compression for swelling and pain. NMES for quadriceps after TKA may help early strength [Ref – to verify].
Range, TUG, 30 s chair stand, 6MWT, stair climb test, Oxford Knee or Hip Score, KOOS or HOOS.

items: **Why mobilise on the day of surgery or day 1?** Reduces complications and speeds recovery.
**Which motion is commonly hardest to regain after TKA?** Flexion, and full extension if not prioritised.
**What is a sign of hip abductor weakness?** Trendelenburg gait.
**Why do precautions differ between patients after THA?** They depend on surgical approach and surgeon preference.
**Sudden hip pain with shortened leg after bending?** Suspected dislocation.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Prescribe range and strength programs for TKA and THA.
